answer_text:
We solve the real equation

\[
4^{x-1}=9x^{3-x}+7.
\]

Since \(x^{3-x}\) is involved, we consider real solutions with \(x>0\).

First, test \(x=3\):

\[
4^{3-1}=4^2=16
\]

and

\[
9\cdot 3^{3-3}+7=9\cdot 3^0+7=9+7=16.
\]

So \(x=3\) is a solution.

Now we show it is the only solution.

### Case 1: \(0<x<1\)

Then \(x-1<0\), so

\[
4^{x-1}<1.
\]

Also, \(x^{3-x}>0\), so

\[
9x^{3-x}+7>7.
\]

Thus the left side is less than \(1\), while the right side is greater than \(7\), so there is no solution in \((0,1)\).

### Case 2: \(1\le x<3\)

Here \(x-1<2\), so

\[
4^{x-1}<16.
\]

Also, since \(x\ge 1\) and \(3-x>0\),

\[
x^{3-x}\ge 1.
\]

Therefore,

\[
9x^{3-x}+7\ge 16.
\]

At \(x=1\), the left side is \(1\), not \(16\). For \(1<x<3\), we have strict inequalities:

\[
4^{x-1}<16 \le 9x^{3-x}+7.
\]

So there is no solution in \([1,3)\).

### Case 3: \(x>3\)

Then \(x-1>2\), so

\[
4^{x-1}>16.
\]

Also, since \(x>1\) and \(3-x<0\),

\[
x^{3-x}<1.
\]

Thus

\[
9x^{3-x}+7<16.
\]

So the left side is greater than \(16\), while the right side is less than \(16\). Hence there is no solution for \(x>3\).

The only real solution is therefore

\[
\boxed{3}
\]
